findings.summary: QuickSearch carries a second global `s` shortcut guard that is weaker than the shell shortcut policy.
findings.consequence: The current SiteShell caller already opens QuickSearch from the shared production shortcut handler, so this component-level listener is redundant there. If the component is mounted standalone, its local guard can still intercept modified `s` keystrokes or keystrokes inside contenteditable regions, unlike the established `isProductionShortcutGuarded` policy.
findings.evidence: The owned line 259 guards only `input, textarea, select`. The direct caller `app/components/global/SiteShell.vue` opens `LazyQuickSearch` from `onShellKeydown`, which calls `isProductionShortcutGuarded`; that shared guard also rejects modifier keys, composition, dialogs, and `[contenteditable]` targets in `app/lib/production-shortcuts.ts`. The packet unit's `onMounted` listener therefore duplicates the shell behavior but does not preserve the same policy boundary.
findings.recommendation: Delete the component-level global keydown listener if QuickSearch is only opened through SiteShell. If standalone global opening is intentional, delegate `onGlobalKeydown` to `isProductionShortcutGuarded(event)` before checking `event.key === "s"`.
